statement: Let total = m*n, k = (total - 1)/2, and let flat be the list of length total obtained by sorting, in non-decreasing order, all entries grid[i][j] (0 <= i < m, 0 <= j < n) counted with multiplicity. The function returns a result r and r = flat[k] (0-indexed), i.e. r is the k-th smallest matrix entry counted with multiplicity. Equivalently, at most k entries are strictly less than r and at most k entries are strictly greater than r.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid) and n = len(grid[i]) for each i (all rows of grid have common length n). Assume 1 <= m <= 500, 1 <= n <= 500, m is odd, n is odd, each row grid[i] is sorted in non-decreasing order (grid[i][j] <= grid[i][j+1] for all 0 <= j < n-1), and 1 <= grid[i][j] <= 1000000 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.
